scope: Topic census of every ACM SIGCOMM main-track title listed in the official programmes for 2022-2026. This extends program-screen.json, which classified only three buckets, to a full fourteen-category breakdown so the conference's topic mix can be ranked.
method: two independent coders every year; all 17 disagreements adjudicated by a third agent, five of them against the paper's abstract; one correction (CoOrbit) from the official session listing

categories.ai-infra: The network, fabric, transport, scheduling or state movement serving a machine-learning training or inference workload.
categories.ml-for-networking: Machine learning used as a technique to run, configure, diagnose or analyse a network.
categories.datacenter-transport: Datacenter transport and host networking that is not machine-learning specific.
categories.dc-topology-optics: Datacenter topology and reconfigurable optics, not specific to a machine-learning workload.
categories.wan-routing-te: Wide-area and inter-domain networking, traffic engineering, routing.
categories.measurement: Measuring or diagnosing networks and the Internet.
categories.verification-config: Formal verification, configuration analysis, testing and correctness tooling.
categories.wireless-cellular: Wireless and mobile substrates, including aerial radio.
categories.satellite-ntn: Satellite, LEO, orbital or non-terrestrial substrate.
categories.video-web-qoe: Video streaming, conferencing, content delivery, quality of experience.
categories.other: Anything the categories above do not fit.

caveats: Denominators are the title rows on the official page for each year; the 2022-2023 pages are programme pages and the 2024-2026 pages are accepted-paper pages, so the five denominators are not identically constructed.

Classification is title-level except where a disagreement forced an abstract or session check. A title can hide its workload: CoOrbit carries no satellite word and was corrected from its session placement.

The satellite column reproduces the independently verified census 1/0/0/6/4. Loon and the low-altitude UAV study are non-terrestrial but not satellite, and sit in wireless-cellular; folding them in gives 2/0/0/6/5.

Two category boundaries are genuinely contested and were decided on the abstract: Artic, real-time communication for a multimodal-model consumer, is counted as ai-infra although its official session is Learning-Based & Data-Driven Network Systems; SCX, a key-value cache encoding, is counted as security-privacy for its confidentiality objective. Under the narrower AI-datacenter-fabric reading the 2026 ai-infra count is 29 rather than 30.
